use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

claims.content: The C2 JU reports air and surface surveillance tracks to the interface in accordance with track reporting, correlation, positional data, velocity, and identity data exchange requirements.

goal.raw_text: The C2 JU reports air and surface surveillance tracks to the interface in accordance with track reporting, correlation, positional data, velocity, and identity data exchange requirements.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C2 JU has a capability to originate and report real-time air or surface tracks.
The C2 JU has a capability to perform common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria.
The C2 JU has an automatic correlation capability.
The C2 JU has an automatic decorrelation capability.
The C2 JU is capable of assuming R2 for air, surface, or land tracks.
The C2 JU has achieved Active status, or has returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration have been performed.
The minimum wait of 12 seconds before reporting air and surface tracks has elapsed.
The C2 JU originates and reports a real-time air or surface track to the interface.

trigger.raw_text: The C2 JU originates and reports a real-time air or surface track to the interface.

claims.content: The C2 JU originates and reports a real-time air or surface track.
The C2 JU performs common tracking in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria, which differ depending on the E/C of the tracks.
The C2 JU compares locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

The C2 JU determines the C2 JU responsible for reporting the tracked object in accordance with the Air, Surface, Land, and Space Surveillance sections; the tracked object normally is reported by one C2 JU while other C2 JUs withhold their reports.
The C2 JU periodically compares remote tracks to local tracks to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
When the C2 JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action, either automatically or manually.
The C2 JU reports air surveillance data using the J3.2 message and surface surveillance data using the J3.3 message.
The C2 JU reports air surveillance data including Altitude and Altitude Source when available.
The C2 JU reports velocity as course and speed, with speed in data miles per hour of ground speed and course in degrees with respect to true north.
The C2 JU exchanges track identity as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1, including platform and platform activity fields.

If the C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has R2, it transmits the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, except when it ceases reporting because it has relinquished R2 to another JU or when that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.
C2 JUs may also perform manual decorrelation, and may have a capability to require manual confirmation of automatic decorrelations.

If the Dropped TN had the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1. If the Dropped TN had the Emergency Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN shall have the Emergency Indicator set to value 1.

If the RV field is set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected. Receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine if a reverse correlation request should be originated or if the original correlation request should be rejected.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection.
When the RV field is set to value 3, it indicates the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection.

If the C2 JU has R2, it reports all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in the J3.2C1 and J3.3C1 words for Air and Surface tracks, respectively, in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages; if the C2 JU does not have R2, it monitors IFF/SIF surveillance data and only reports if it holds different data with the J7.5 message.
Whenever a correlation request is rejected, the C2 JU transmits the J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 to report the rejection. Exit: the rejection is reported to the interface.

If the RV field is set to value 1, it indicates a reverse correlation request would be rejected; receiving IUs desiring to reverse the requested correlation use the RV field to determine whether a reverse correlation request should be originated or whether the original correlation request should be rejected. Exit: the receiving IU originates a reverse correlation request or rejects the original correlation request accordingly.

When the RV field is set to value 3, the correlation was manually initiated and shall be accepted unless certain conditions apply which require rejection. Exit: the manual correlation is accepted, or if rejection is required, the correlation request is rejected and reported.

Air surveillance tracks have been reported using the J3.2 message (PTI=1), surface surveillance tracks have been reported using the J3.3 message (PTI=1), and these messages are available to non-C2 JUs for situational awareness and early warning information.
Reported air surveillance data includes Altitude and Altitude Source when available.
The velocity of reported air and surface tracks is reported as course and speed, with speed in data miles per hour of ground speed and course in degrees with respect to true north.
Track identity is exchanged as defined in paragraph 4.4.2.1, including platform and platform activity fields implemented by the C2 JU.
Common tracking has been performed in accordance with the correlation and decorrelation procedures and criteria, which differ depending on the E/C of the tracks.
Correlation has been performed by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with data received on the interface to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

Recognition and resolution of air and surface track dual designations have been performed by periodically comparing remote tracks to local tracks, and action has been initiated, either automatically or manually, when two reported tracks are eligible for correlation.

If a Dropped TN had the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN has the Force Tell Indicator set to value 1; if the Dropped TN had the Emergency Indicator set to value 1, the Retained TN has the Emergency Indicator set to value 1.
